headline: High-risk default filesystem and browser overlap creates prompt-injection, leakage, and action-cascade exposure between CrewAI and ctx.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and run browsers, while ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and uses MCP stdio. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled files or tool outputs from one side can influence the other. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes untrusted content into the shared working directory
IF ctx ingests Claude Code tool-event content without provenance filtering
IF both are connected through an MCP or file-based bridge
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable automatic parsing of file contents as instructions
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts
Restrict ctx to read-only observation of tool events
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys and broad network egress, and ctx touches audit/runtime logs plus harness records and MCP servers. If they share a workspace or logs, sensitive crew data can flow into ctx outputs or external APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred and escalated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or log directory
IF CrewAI stores secrets or crew data in files ctx can read
IF ctx forwards observed records into GitHub, Claude Code, or other APIs
mitigations: Use separate directories and log sinks
Redact secrets before writing any shared artifact
Turn off verbose runtime logging for shared runs
Restrict ctx to metadata-only observation
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has write_filesystem, execute_shell, subprocesses, and broad network egress; ctx has filesystem access and can call GitHub, GitHub Actions, MkDocs Material, and Claude Code. Even without explicit git-write on ctx, both can mutate shared files and external automation targets, so concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other. Uncertainty about locking means the safer high rating applies.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem tree
IF ctx writes files while CrewAI is also modifying them
IF either agent triggers external automation against the same repository or workspace
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on the same workspace
Review and gate any GitHub/GitHub Actions writes
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate tool outputs and act through subprocesses and APIs, while ctx observes Claude Code events and is positioned to treat those outputs as context. If ctx forwards A's output into downstream actions or documentation without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect commits, automation, or operational decisions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default orchestration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ctx uses CrewAI outputs as authoritative input
IF downstream actions are triggered from observed tool events
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted between agents
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action
Require citations or checksums on transferred facts
Limit ctx to monitoring, not acting
Add human approval for commits or external calls
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and broad network egress, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs, harness records, and graph data and can call GitHub/GitHub Actions. That combination can create retention or residency mismatches if regulated data is present. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR boundaries, so the risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into CrewAI inputs or ctx logs
IF logs or records are retained longer than policy allows
IF GitHub or other external services receive data subject to residency constraints
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Shorten log retention to the minimum needed
Mask secrets before export
Review external API destinations before enabling them
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
